# A stated `cost_basis_balance:` finer than the currency, behind a widened
# `fraction:`.
#
# The amount is a whole number of cents, so the rule on `amount:` passes. The
# balance is not — and the rule on *it* read the commodity this file had just
# restated, so 60.001 USD was accepted and written.
#
# Reopened, USD is a hundredth again and the book holds a basis balance it
# cannot express. Nothing looks at it: `fx-balances` renders it at the
# currency's own places so it displays 60.00, and `--verify-costs` only asks
# whether the balance is between zero and what arrived. The export writes
# `cost_basis_balance: "60.001"` back out, and importing that file without the
# fraction line is refused — a book this tool cannot get out and back in.
2026-01-01 commodity USD
	mnemonic: "USD"
	fullname: "US Dollar"
	namespace: "CURRENCY"
	fraction: 1000
2026-01-01 open Assets
	type: Asset
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank:USD
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
	commodity_scu: 1000

2026-01-10 * "Buy 100 USD at 1.35"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:Bank:USD 100.00 USD
		share_price: "1.35"
		value: "135.00"
		cost_basis_balance: "60.001"
	Assets:Bank -135.00 CAD
